additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.

subtypes.Self-Induced Vomiting: Intentionally inducing vomiting to remove ingested food.
subtypes.Misuse of Medications: Repetitively misusing laxatives, diuretics, or enemas for the purpose of weight control.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

info.persona: Agustin Gonzalez is a curious, organized multitasker who bridges science and art, channeling a love for wildlife and rhythm into community‑focused conservation and creative expression, all while juggling a meticulous budget, occasional back‑aches, and a penchant for late‑night guitar jams.
info.professional_persona: Agustin Gonzalez is a meticulous animal caretaker at a Chicago wildlife rescue center, blending his STEM‑trained precision in veterinary first aid and systematic behavioral observation with a vivid artistic eye for scientific illustration, and they leverage their bilingual fluency and curiosity to translate complex animal health data into engaging, community‑focused outreach programs.
info.cultural_background: Agustín is a first‑generation Cuban‑American; his parents emigrated from Havana in the early 1990s. He grew up bilingual, celebrating Cuban traditions such as Santería music, Carnaval, and family meals centered around dishes like arroz con pollo and platanos maduros. Living in Evergreen Park, IL, he blends his Caribbean heritage with Midwestern life, actively participating in events organized by the Chicago Cuban Cultural Center. His cultural identity fuels his appreciation for rhythm, color, and community, which he channels into his artistic hobbies and his desire to create bilingual outreach programs that resonate with both Spanish‑speaking and English‑speaking audiences.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his free time, Agustín indulges in sketching and painting animals, often using charcoal and watercolor to capture subtle details. He enjoys wildlife photography, especially in Chicago’s forest preserves, and volunteers at a local community garden where he helps create pollinator habitats. An avid reader, he devours popular science and art history books and regularly attends museum exhibitions and gallery openings. He loves cooking traditional Cuban dishes like ropa vieja while listening to Afro‑Cuban jazz. Occasionally, he plays guitar in neighborhood jam sessions and participates in a local soccer league. When seeking solitude, he hikes the Palos Trail System, but he also values social interaction at local art meet‑ups and cultural festivals.
info.sports_persona: Agustin Gonzalez is a regular participant in a co‑ed amateur soccer league that meets on weekday evenings, a devoted follower of the Chicago Cubs during baseball season, and a weekend runner on the Palos Trail System, balancing their fitness routine with occasional pickup basketball games at the local community center.
info.arts_persona: Agustin Gonzalez immerses themselves in the vibrant rhythms of Afro‑Latin jazz, regularly jamming on acoustic guitar to the sounds of Arturo O’Farrill and Tito Puente, while their sketchbooks echo the brushstrokes of Diego Rivera and the chiaroscuro of Caravaggio, and they frequent the Art Institute of Chicago’s modern art exhibitions and local gallery openings.
info.travel_persona: Agustin Gonzalez prefers off‑the‑beaten‑path eco‑travel, planning trips around bird‑watching seasons in Costa Rica’s Monteverde Cloud Forest and the wildlife corridors of the Galápagos, while also cherishing spontaneous weekend getaways to the historic streets of New Orleans and the art‑laden neighborhoods of Santa Fe.
info.culinary_persona: Agustin Gonzalez is a confident home chef who perfects slow‑cooked shredded beef stew (ropa vieja) with cumin, garlic, and a splash of adobo, pairs it with fragrant rice and sweet fried plantains, and enjoys experimenting with fresh cilantro, lime, and a dash of smoked paprika while listening to Afro‑Latin jazz.

info.persona: Lucy Dineen, an organized and talkative automotive aficionado, blends Southern hospitality with a relentless curiosity for emerging tech, they never leave home without a spare wrench, and they fuel both their garage and community gatherings with unwavering enthusiasm.
info.professional_persona: Lucy Dineen, a veteran automotive service technician, leverages deep expertise in engine diagnostics, transmission repair, and hybrid‑electric systems while they enforce rigorous safety protocols and enliven the workshop with their talkative, mentorship‑driven approach.
info.cultural_background: Lucy grew up in a small, close‑knit town in central Arkansas, raised in a white Southern family with Protestant Christian values. Her upbringing emphasized hard work, self‑reliance, and community service, traditions that remain central to her identity. She was shaped by the rural rhythms of agricultural life, local high‑school sports, church gatherings, and regional celebrations that value hospitality and practical skills. While firmly rooted in these Southern cultural touchstones, Lucy also embraces modern influences through ongoing automotive training and a curiosity for new technology, balancing respect for established methods with an openness to innovation.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside the garage, Lucy is an active participant in her community and enjoys a mix of hands‑on and social pursuits. She frequently attends local car shows and swap meets, where she shares her knowledge and connects with fellow enthusiasts. Gardening her vegetable patch and experimenting with Southern comfort food allow her to unwind and host lively dinner gatherings for friends and family. Her love of music spans classic rock and country, often enjoyed while road‑tripping on scenic Arkansas highways. Lucy also volunteers at her church, sings in the choir, engages in DIY woodworking projects for her workshop, reads automotive magazines and tech blogs, and spends weekends fishing or hunting in the nearby countryside.
info.sports_persona: Lucy Dineen spends weekends fishing the Arkansas River and hunting white‑tailed deer with the Lonoke Hunters Association, and they cheer on the Arkansas Razorbacks football team each fall, follow the St. Louis Cardinals during baseball season, and occasionally join a local pickup softball league, blending competitive spirit with relaxed outdoor recreation.
info.arts_persona: Lucy Dineen channels creative energy through woodworking projects for the garage, sings gospel‑infused classics by Johnny Cash and Dolly Parton in the church choir, and they unwind to the riffs of Lynyrd Skynyrd and the storytelling of Bruce Springsteen while hosting themed car‑show evenings that celebrate both mechanical and aesthetic craftsmanship.
info.travel_persona: Lucy Dineen prefers self‑planned road trips that thread scenic Arkansas backroads with pit stops at automotive museums in Detroit and Stuttgart, and they have already toured Nashville’s country‑music venues, taken a weekend hunting expedition to the Texas Hill Country, and dream of exploring Italy’s vintage car collections in Turin, balancing a love of adventure with a budget‑conscious approach.
info.culinary_persona: Lucy Dineen delights in cooking Southern comfort staples such as fried catfish, chicken and dumplings, collard greens, and buttery cornbread, often seasoning with garden‑fresh dill and thyme, and they proudly present low‑and‑slow smoked brisket at community potlucks, though they occasionally indulge in a late‑night slice of pepperoni pizza after a long shift.

info.persona: Retter Pierre blends meticulous accounting precision with a soulful love for music, fishing, and food, channeling community values into a steady, detail‑oriented life marked by disciplined budgeting, diligent health monitoring, and a habit of lingering over a good mystery novel while the woodshop timer clicks.
info.professional_persona: Retter Pierre is a seasoned bookkeeping and auditing clerk with over three decades of experience who leverages meticulous ledger management, deep knowledge of Georgia tax law, and pragmatic curiosity to mentor junior staff while gradually shifting toward a supervisory role, and they are actively pursuing a Certified Bookkeeper credential to formalize their expertise.
info.cultural_background: Maurice identifies as African‑American with a family lineage that includes Haitian ancestors, a heritage reflected in his name and occasional culinary traditions. He was raised in a close‑knit, church‑centered neighborhood in DeKalb County during the 1970s and 1980s, a period when the Black community in Atlanta was forging new economic and political pathways. The values of perseverance, mutual aid, and respect for elders that he learned from his church and extended family continue to shape his worldview. He participates in community events such as Juneteenth celebrations, local civil‑rights commemorations, and the annual Haitian Heritage Festival in the Atlanta area. His cultural identity blends Southern African‑American customs—soul food, gospel music, storytelling—with the Creole influences of his Haitian forebears, creating a rich personal tapestry that informs both his professional ethic and his community involvement.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Maurice enjoys spending quiet mornings fishing at Lake Sidney Lanier and taking weekend hikes on the trails of Stone Mountain Park. He is an avid fan of classic soul and gospel music, often attending services and choir rehearsals at his local Baptist church. He loves preparing Southern comfort foods—especially collard greens, fried catfish, and sweet potato pie—while experimenting with occasional Haitian dishes that reflect his family’s roots. Maurice also follows the Atlanta Hawks and Falcons, participates in a weekly community gardening club, and reads historical non‑fiction, particularly works on African‑American history and civil‑rights movements. When he needs solitary downtime, he reads mystery novels or works on a small woodworking project he started after retiring his first car.
info.sports_persona: Retter Pierre is a devoted supporter of the Atlanta Hawks and Atlanta Falcons, regularly attending Hawks games at State Farm Arena and cheering on the Falcons during Sunday night football, while they also organize friendly pick‑up soccer matches for the community gardening club at the local park and they keep fit by hiking Stone Mountain trails.
info.arts_persona: Retter Pierre is a lifelong aficionado of classic soul and gospel, filling the house with Marvin Gaye, Aretha Franklin, and the stirring harmonies of local Baptist choir rehearsals, and they regularly attend performances at the Fox Theatre, explore folk art exhibitions at the High Museum, and unwind with mystery novels by Agatha Christie.
info.travel_persona: Retter Pierre favors low‑key, nature‑focused getaways, planning weekend fishing trips to Lake Sidney Lanier and hiking excursions in the Appalachians, while they have already explored historic Savannah and New Orleans for culinary inspiration and they dream of a cultural pilgrimage to Port‑au‑Prince to connect with family recipes, balancing travel budgets with their retirement planning.
info.culinary_persona: Retter Pierre delights in cooking Southern comfort fare—smoky collard greens, crisp fried catfish, and sweet potato pie—while occasionally mastering Haitian classics like griot and rice‑and‑beans, and they relish experimenting with seasonings such as allspice, scotch bonnet peppers, and fresh okra from their modest kitchen garden.
